expected_output.reasoning: The agent's response correctly identifies inode exhaustion as the root cause, explains that df -h shows byte usage while df -i shows inode usage, and that massive numbers of small files (PHP sessions, mail queue, tmp, logs) can consume all inodes while leaving plenty of byte-space free. It provides the exact df -i command to confirm, a find-based command to locate directories with the most files, and cleanup commands targeting /tmp, PHP sessions, postfix maildrop, package cache, and old logs — matching all key elements of the expected output almost exactly.

Common culprits: a stuck Postfix mail queue, PHP session files that were never garbage-collected, or Docker layers... find /tmp -type f -mtime +3 -delete ... find /var/lib/php/sessions ... find /var/spool/postfix/maildrop ..."

assertion_results.evidence: The output repeatedly uses the word 'inode', e.g. 'your filesystem has run out of inodes, not disk space.'

assertion_results.text: Identifies inode exhaustion (not byte-level disk full) as the cause given df -h shows free space
assertion_results.evidence: The agent explicitly states: 'What's actually wrong: your filesystem has run out of inodes, not disk space... df -h only reports block/byte usage, so it can show 55% free while df -i shows 100% inode usage.' This directly identifies inode exhaustion as the cause despite df -h showing free space.

assertion_results.text: Recommends checking df -i and freeing large numbers of small files
assertion_results.evidence: The agent recommends running 'df -i / /var /tmp' to confirm, then provides a find-based script to locate directories with millions of small files, and cleanup commands like 'find /tmp -type f -mtime +3 -delete', 'find /var/lib/php/sessions -type f -mtime +1 -delete', etc., which free large numbers of small files to reclaim inodes.

assertion_results.text: Distinguishes freeing inodes from freeing disk bytes
assertion_results.evidence: The agent explicitly distinguishes the two: 'df -h only reports block/byte usage, so it can show 55% free while df -i shows 100% inode usage,' and frames the fix as freeing inodes (deleting many small files) rather than freeing disk bytes, explicitly noting 'Clean up (safe, non-destructive to app data)' targeting file counts, not disk space.
